## Revenue up 80% year over year; Signed a new non-binding LOI for 118 MW at Kati; Partnership with Applied Digital at Dorothy 3; Kati 1 delivered (83 MW); Generate Capital debt fully repaid


**ALBANY, NY, November 16, 2026 –** Soluna Holdings, Inc. (“Soluna” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: SLNH), a developer of green data centers for intensive computing applications, including artificial intelligence and high-performance computing, announced its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


“Our focus is converting the AI projects in our pipeline to signed leases,” said John Belizaire, CEO of Soluna Holdings. “In recent months, we advanced development and initial construction at Kati 2 and Dorothy 3. We received ERCOT Base Load classifications for 266 megawatts across our two Texas campuses, and closed on the Dorothy 3 land. In October, we signed a subscription agreement with Applied Digital for a planned 50-megawatt AI data center at Dorothy 3. In November, we signed a non-binding letter of intent with a new prospective tenant for 118 MW at Kati 2. Our priorities now are securing definitive leases, arranging project financing and advancing both projects toward delivery. We are committed to developing these projects responsibly and working with local communities as they progress.”


“Our third-quarter results reflect continued revenue growth, despite $3.0 million in unplanned turbine repair expenses and related downtime at the Briscoe Wind Farm. Completing the wind farm integration and associated turbine upgrades positions the asset for improved operational performance and supports our AI strategy at Dorothy 3,” Belizaire continued. “We exited the quarter with $109 million in cash and, subsequent to quarter-end, fully repaid our Generate Capital debt, strengthening our balance sheet and enhancing financial flexibility as we advance our AI infrastructure development pipeline.”


Conceptual rendering of Soluna’s project Dorothy 3


**Recent Highlights:**


**Advanced AI strategy and project execution**


- **Project Kati 2 / AI –** After the prior prospective tenant’s exclusivity period ended, Soluna remarketed the site and, in November, signed a non-binding letter of intent with a new prospective tenant to lease 118 IT MW


at the planned 350+ MW Kati 2 campus.


- **Project Dorothy 3 / AI –** Acquired 397 acres on August 24 for the planned 300 MW renewable-first AI campus. On October 20, Soluna signed a subscription agreement to form a joint venture, 51% Applied Digital and 49% Soluna, for a planned 50 MW critical IT Phase 1 AI/HPC facility at Dorothy 3. ChronoScale signed a non-binding letter of intent to lease the facility. Closing is expected by year-end 2026, subject to remaining conditions.


- **Kati 2 and Dorothy 3 construction –** Construction began at both sites in October.


- **Power and interconnection –** Received ERCOT Base Load classifications in September covering 266 MW of existing interconnection capacity across the Kati (166 MW), including the planned Kati 2 expansion) and Dorothy (100 MW) campuses. These classifications preserve existing capacity and exempt it from further reliability evaluation and megawatt allocation in the Batch Zero study, pending completion of ERCOT’s verification process. An additional 50 MW request at Dorothy is under study.


- **Tax exemptions and abatement –** Soluna received sales and use tax exemptions for Projects Kati 2 and Dorothy 3. On November 9, 2026, the Briscoe County Commissioners Court approved a Chapter 312 tax abatement agreement for Phase 1 of Dorothy 3.


- **Project Kati 1 –** Completed the final 14 MW on September 8, fully energizing the 83 MW site. Revenue from the newly energized K1BC phase was first recognized in Q3. A substation outage in mid-September temporarily affected part of the site.


**Strengthened the balance sheet and financial flexibility**


- **Liquidity and capital formation –** Soluna ended the quarter with $109.3 million in unrestricted cash and $16.7 million in total debt, net of issuance costs. Soluna raised $37.7 million through its ATM program in Q3, funding the August Generate prepayment, capex, and operations.


- **Generate Capital debt fully repaid –** In August, Soluna prepaid its Generate facilities at Dorothy 1A and Dorothy 2 for $19.1 million. On October 22, 2026, Soluna repaid the remaining balance of its Generate Capital credit facility, which had helped finance the April 2026 acquisition of the Briscoe Wind Farm. Together, these repayments completed the payoff of the $27.5 million of principal outstanding at June 30, 2026. The facility has been terminated, and Generate’s liens on the project assets have been released, reducing total debt principal from $37.9 million at June 30, 2026 to $7.7 million following the October repayment.


- **Authorized share increase –** At the Company’s 2026 annual meeting of stockholders held on October 16, 2026, Soluna’s stockholders approved an increase in the Company’s authorized common stock from 375 million to 1.0 billion shares and the issuance of shares above Nasdaq’s 20% limit under the Yorkville SEPA.


**Expanded leadership and internal AI capability**


- **Leadership and team –** Ryan Carver joined as Chief Development Officer in July to lead AI infrastructure development. He has since built out the development team, bringing on Neil Robinson as Vice President of Construction and Michal Stark as Vice President of Procurement.


- **Board election –** At the Company’s 2026 annual meeting of stockholders held on October 16, 2026, Soluna’s stockholders elected Dan Golding to the Company’s Board of Directors. Dan brings more than 30 years of experience in data centers and digital infrastructure, including leadership roles at Google and Iron Mountain.


**Third Quarter Financial Highlights:**


- **Revenue grew 80% over Q3 2025 to $15.1 million** (29% excluding the gross presentation of pass-through electricity), marking a sixth consecutive quarter of sequential growth.


Hosting capacity additions, contract termination revenue, and new wind generation revenue from Briscoe were partially offset by a 37% decline in average hashprice, which reduced proprietary mining and profit-share hosting revenue.


- **Gross profit decreased to a loss of (** **$-1.9) million** **from a profit of** **$2.3 million in Q3 2025** **,** mainly due to $3.0 million of unscheduled turbine repairs at Briscoe Wind Farm. Excluding the repairs, gross profit would have been $1.1 million.


- **Net loss increased to $** **-34.3 million** **from $** **-25.8 million** **in Q3 2025.** **** The absence of a $22.0 million fair value adjustment loss recorded in Q3 2025 was partially offset by a $15.8 million unfavorable change in debt extinguishment (a loss on the Generate prepayment in 2026 compared with a gain on the NYDIG settlement in 2025), a $14.0 million increase in non-cash stock-based compensation, and $3.1 million of higher cash G&A. Other movements included a $4.2 million decline in gross profit and a $4.7 million reduction in other financing expense.


- **Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to** **$-7.5 million** **from** **$-6.4 million** **in Q3 2025,** driven by the Briscoe turbine repairs and higher G&A reflecting continued investment in the HPC business, mainly legal and consulting fees for Kati 2 development and new site evaluation, partially offset by the absence of prior-year financing costs. Reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to net loss, the most comparable GAAP financial metric, is in the Appendix.


- **Unrestricted cash was $109.3 million at September 30, 2026, up 43% from $76.4 million at year-end 2025,** available to fund future development.


- **Deleveraged while funding growth.** The $170.1 million raised year-to-date through the ATM and SEPA funded the Briscoe Wind acquisition, project capex, buyouts of the JV partners at Dorothy 1A and 1B, and $40.5 million of debt repayments, including the August Generate prepayment, reducing total debt to $16.7 million at quarter-end from $26.8 million at year-end 2025. Following the October repayment of the remaining Generate balance, total debt principal is approximately $7.7 million.

**Non-GAAP Measures**


In addition to figures prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), Soluna from time to time may present alternative non-GAAP performance measures, e.g., EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net profit/loss, adjusted earnings per share, free cash flow, both on a company basis and on a project-level basis, among others. EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, and depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as EBITDA adjusted for stock-based compensation costs, loss on sale of fixed assets and deposit on equipment, right of first refusal amortization gain, accretion of asset retirement obligation, SEPA commitment fee, fair value adjustment loss, and gain on debt extinguishment and revaluation, net. Project-level measures may not take into account a full allocation of corporate expenses. These measures should be considered in addition to, but not as a substitute for, the information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Alternative performance measures are not subject to GAAP or any other generally accepted accounting principles. Other companies may define these terms in different ways. **About Soluna Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLNH)**


Soluna is on a mission to make renewable energy a global superpower using computing as a catalyst. The company designs, develops, and operates digital infrastructure that transforms surplus renewable energy into global computing resources. Soluna’s pioneering data centers are strategically co-located with wind, solar, or hydroelectric power plants to support high-performance computing applications, including Bitcoin Mining, Generative AI, and other compute-intensive applications. Soluna’s proprietary software MaestroOS(™) helps energize a greener grid while delivering cost-effective and sustainable computing solutions and superior returns. To learn more, visit
